nodes.description: State variable holding the reference to the external BIT/8thereum token contract.
State variable holding the address of the contract owner.
Boolean state flag controlling whether the game can be played.
State variable storing the pseudo-random winning number for each round.
Mapping tracking the amount already paid/entered per player address.
Constructor initializing BITcontract, openToPublic and owner.
Main game entry point: verifies payment, derives winning number and pays the winner.
View helper returning the BIT token balance of an arbitrary address.
View helper reading how many tokens a player has paid to the game contract.
View function returning half of the contract BIT balance.
View function returning the BIT balance of a fixed whale address.
Owner-only function enabling public game play.
Owner-only trapdoor to rescue arbitrary ERC20 tokens held by the contract.
Modifier restricting execution to the contract owner.
Modifier preventing the BIT token contract from being passed as the rescue target.
Modifier requiring the openToPublic flag to be true.
Modifier requiring msg.sender to equal tx.origin.
Caller-controlled address used for ownership checks, randomness and payouts.
Transaction origin used in the anti-contract check.
Access control check require(msg.sender == owner) inside onlyOwner.
Check require(aContract != address(BITcontract)) inside notBIT.
Check require(openToPublic) inside isOpenToPublic.
Weak anti-bot check require(msg.sender == tx.origin) inside onlyRealPeople.
owner = msg.sender assignment performed in the constructor.
winningNumber = uint256(keccak256(blockhash(block.number-1), choice, msg.sender))%5 +1, a block-dependent pseudo-random derivation.
External call BITcontract.transfer(msg.sender, tokensToWinner) paying the winner.
External call ERC20Interface(tokenAddress).transfer(tokenOwner, tokens) inside returnAnyERC20Token.
tokensToWinner = (BITBalanceOf(address(this)) / 2) division determining the payout size.
State write paidPlayers[msg.sender] = tokensTransferred.
State write openToPublic = true enabling public play.
revert() executed when the player has not paid into the game.
Arithmetic return balance / 2 computing the winners pot.
Player-supplied number parameter choice of start(uint256 choice).
Address parameter someAddress of BITBalanceOf.
Address parameter customerAddress of getTokensPaidToGame.
Token contract address parameter tokenAddress of returnAnyERC20Token.
Recipient parameter tokenOwner of returnAnyERC20Token.
Amount parameter tokens of returnAnyERC20Token.
Address parameter aContract of the notBIT modifier.
Local flag didYouWin initialised to false in start.
Local variable tokensTransferred holding getTokensPaidToGame(msg.sender).
Local variable tokensToWinner holding half of the contract balance.
Local variable balance in winnersPot holding BITBalanceOf(this).
Local variable balance in BITWhaleBalance holding the whale balance.

edges.reason: Constructor assigns the BITcontract state variable.
Constructor sets the openToPublic flag to false.
Constructor executes the owner assignment operation.
start applies the isOpenToPublic modifier.
start applies the onlyRealPeople modifier.
start calls getTokensPaidToGame to read the player payment.
start writes the paidPlayers mapping for the caller.
start computes the pseudo-random winning number.
start calls BITBalanceOf to size the payout.
start computes tokensToWinner by dividing the balance.
start performs the external BIT transfer to the winner.
start reverts when the player has not paid into the game.
openToThePublic is guarded by the onlyOwner modifier.
openToThePublic sets openToPublic to true.
returnAnyERC20Token is guarded by the onlyOwner modifier.
returnAnyERC20Token is guarded by the notBIT modifier.
returnAnyERC20Token performs an external ERC20 transfer.
winnersPot calls BITBalanceOf(this).
winnersPot divides the balance by two.
BITWhaleBalance calls BITBalanceOf for the whale address.
onlyOwner executes the ownership require.
notBIT executes the BIT contract address require.
isOpenToPublic enforces the openToPublic flag require.
onlyRealPeople enforces msg.sender == tx.origin.
msg.sender is compared against owner in the access control check.
owner state variable is the trusted side of the ownership check.
msg.sender is compared with tx.origin in the anti-bot check.
tx.origin participates in the weak msg.sender == tx.origin check.
msg.sender is written as the contract owner.
The owner assignment writes the owner state variable.
msg.sender is hashed into the block-dependent random number.
Player-supplied choice feeds the pseudo-random derivation.
The computed pseudo-random value is stored into winningNumber.
The winningNumber comparison gates whether the payout transfer executes.
BITcontract is used to query the token balance.
BITcontract is used to query gamePlayers.
BITcontract is the external contract invoked for the winner payout.
BITcontract address is compared inside notBIT.
openToPublic flag is read by the require statement.
msg.sender is passed as the player address to getTokensPaidToGame.
The external payment query result is stored in tokensTransferred.
tokensTransferred is written into paidPlayers.
msg.sender is used as the mapping key of the state write.
paidPlayers mapping is updated by the state write.
The state write mutates the paidPlayers mapping.
Contract BIT balance result is used in the division.
The division result is stored in tokensToWinner.
tokensToWinner is passed as the amount of the external transfer.
Tokens are transferred to the caller-controlled address during execution.
The balance query result is stored in the local balance variable.
The local balance is divided by two.
The whale balance query result is stored in the local balance variable.
tokenAddress selects the arbitrary external contract invoked by the transfer.
tokenOwner is used as the recipient of the external transfer.
tokens is used as the amount of the external transfer.
tokenAddress is compared against the BIT contract address in notBIT.
The external BIT transfer can call back into start before state is finalized.
The external ERC20 transfer can call back into returnAnyERC20Token.
